definitions.explanation: The present time, especially when contrasted with the past. A formal expression used to introduce current trends, situations, or changes in society.

examples.japanese: {昨今|さっこん}の{物価|ぶっか}{高|だか}は{深刻|しんこく}だ。
examples.english: The recent rise in prices is serious.

examples.japanese: {昨今|さっこん}、{転職|てんしょく}する{若者|わかもの}が{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: Nowadays, more and more young people are changing jobs.

examples.japanese: {昨今|さっこん}の{技術|ぎじゅつ}{革新|かくしん}は{目覚|めざ}ましく、{生活|せいかつ}のあらゆる{面|めん}に{影響|えいきょう}を{与|あた}えている。
examples.english: Recent technological innovation has been remarkable, affecting every aspect of daily life.

notes:
USAGE:
A formal, written-register word. Used in news articles, essays, and formal speech to discuss current trends or social changes. More literary than {最近|さいきん} (recently) or このごろ (these days). Often appears at the beginning of a sentence to set the temporal frame.

PATTERNS:
- {昨今|さっこん}の + noun: recent/current + noun
- {昨今|さっこん}、… : nowadays, …

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {昨今|さっこん}の{情勢|じょうせい}: the current situation
- {昨今|さっこん}の{事情|じじょう}: recent circumstances
- {昨今|さっこん}の{傾向|けいこう}: recent trends

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {最近|さいきん}: recently (general, everyday)
- このごろ: these days (casual)
- {近年|きんねん}: in recent years (formal, longer timeframe)
